title.en: Desired state, observed state and a reconciliation loop

summary: Model an operator loop where the difference between requested and observed state drives every action taken.
objective: Build a reconciliation view where I can change the desired state, inject drift and watch a controller issue actions until observed matches desired.
intent_signals: Show how a controller keeps a system at its desired state.
Demonstrate drift being corrected by a reconciliation loop.
example_prompts: Build a control loop view with a desired state panel, an observed state panel and a queue of corrective actions.
Let me delete a running unit and watch the controller recreate it.
negative_signals: Not a model of any specific cluster, product or version behaviour.
Not a capacity or scheduling simulator; placement decisions here are illustrative.
not_for: Not a model of any specific cluster, product or version behaviour.
Not a capacity or scheduling simulator; placement decisions here are illustrative.

entities.name: Desired specification
entities.guidance: Show the requested state as an editable specification object, since every action must be traceable to a difference from it.

entities.name: Observed inventory
entities.guidance: Show actual units as separate objects that can be removed or altered outside the controller, so drift can be created deliberately.

entities.name: Action queue
entities.guidance: Queue each corrective action with the difference that produced it, so actions are explained rather than merely animated.

state_contract.model: A desired specification, an observed inventory, a difference computation and a queue of corrective actions applied over discrete ticks. Actions are idempotent in intent: repeating a reconcile with no difference produces no action.
state_contract.authority: The difference between desired and observed is authoritative for every action; no action may be generated from a timer alone.
actions: Delete or corrupt an observed unit to inject drift.
Reset both states to the authored baseline.

invariants: A reconcile tick with no difference enqueues no action.
Every enqueued action names the specific difference that caused it.
Repeated ticks converge toward zero difference or the scene reports that convergence stalled.
Queued actions carry the desired-state generation and resource identity they were derived from; a later edit cancels or revalidates them instead of leaving a stale action to execute.
Reconciling again before a queued action completes does not enqueue a duplicate for the same resource and generation.
motion_guidance: Animate actions taking effect over ticks so the loop is a sequence of observations and responses, not an instant snap.
Show the difference count shrinking as actions complete, since that is the evidence that the loop is working.
known_limits: A teaching loop with immediate, always-successful actions unless failure is injected deliberately.
Real controllers contend with partial failures, rate limits and races that this recipe only gestures at.

A declared tick bound ends the run: if the difference is not resolved within it the scene reports a stalled loop, and failed actions are reported rather than retried forever. No-op when already equal is weaker than idempotent effects under retry, and only the former is modelled.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

claims.statement: A control loop is a non-terminating loop that regulates the state of a system; a controller tracks at least one resource type whose specification represents the desired state, and it makes or requests changes to move the current state closer to that desired state.
claims.scope: Reconciliation framing from official documentation of one platform; the modelled controller here is illustrative.

source_refs.locator: Kubernetes Controllers concept page, control loop and desired state

object_craft.structure: Unit objects on a floor grid with health badges and an identity plate, so removal and recreation are visible events.
object_craft.material: Neutral unit material with a reserved accent for units created during the current reconcile.
object_craft.articulation: Units appear and disappear at tick boundaries rather than continuously.

object_craft.structure: A queue rail with action cards showing the action and its triggering difference.
object_craft.material: Card plates opaque with a distinct treatment for completed and failed actions.
object_craft.articulation: Cards advance along the rail as ticks process them.

physical_contract.scope: Discrete tick-based state changes; no physical transport or contact.
checks: A tick with zero difference produces zero actions.
Injected drift is corrected within a bounded number of ticks or reported as stalled.
